intent.tagline: Three structure signals coach GREEN when it adds a file, and VALIDATE reports them beside the slice score.
intent.narration: An agent adds each new file to the nearest folder. The coach sees one file, and the rubric scores behaviour. This design adds three structure signals to both points. It also makes the main agent use the slice agents.

problem_solution.problem: No part of the slice loop looks at where a file goes or what its name says. The coach reports smells inside one file. The rubric scores behaviour. In some sessions the main agent writes the slice itself, so no coach and no blind score run.
problem_solution.solution: One shared script reports a crowded folder, a name-stem cluster, and a generic file name, only for files that are untracked or added since the merge-base. The coach passes them to GREEN as advice. VALIDATE writes an advisory Structure block. A script checks that the slice agents did the work.
problem_solution.narration: The signals need no parser, so they work in each language. A git comparison with the merge-base is the ratchet, so old debt stays silent. Each limit is advice until a replay evaluation proves an effect.

beats.text: The research synthesis found that guidance at the start lowers the first level of decay, not its rate. Feedback during the write had the best evidence, and the slice loop gives none about structure.
ADR-0025 lets the coach run for the GREEN agent only, and it never blocks a write. The design keeps both rules, so it adds no hook and no agent.
One script, shared/structure_signals.py, is the source of each signal. It prints habit-hooks findings JSON, so the coach, VALIDATE, review mode, and maintenance mode read one format.
VALIDATE writes the Structure block outside the overall score. The rubric has no weights, and an unproven limit must not fail a slice.
The second runner in habit_coach.py is the one route. It keeps the smell check and the structure check apart. A spike shows one real coach message first.
The replay evaluation runs slice plans with the signals on and off. It records the folder growth and the follow-on resolve rate, and it decides what becomes a scored criterion.

alternatives.option: Build a new /architect:refactor command with a graph engine, as the first research run proposed
alternatives.rejected_because: It runs after the damage. The evidence favours feedback at write time, and its thresholds have no source.

alternatives.option: Remove the GREEN filter, so the coach runs for each caller in each session
alternatives.rejected_because: ADR-0025 holds the filter as a rule. Each write in each session then waits on habit-hooks. The engineer kept the filter.

alternatives.option: Add weighted structure criteria S1 to S5 to the rubric at once
alternatives.rejected_because: The rubric has no weights, and a score is a plain average. An unproven threshold can then fail a slice.

alternatives.option: Keep a baseline file of old findings in .cobuilder/
alternatives.rejected_because: A git comparison with the merge-base, with untracked files included, gives the same ratchet. It adds no state file to keep current.

alternatives.option: Add an import check with dependency-cruiser and import-linter in the first version
alternatives.rejected_because: It adds two tool dependencies and covers two languages only. The three signals work in each language.

alternatives.option: Add a PreToolUse speed bump that blocks the first write of a new file
alternatives.rejected_because: It is a fifth hook script and a new event under ADR-0025. No study shows that a block works better than advice.

alternatives.option: Make slice-loop.js the default way to run each slice, so code enforces the agent order
alternatives.rejected_because: It is too heavy for a small build, and each run needs the engineer to opt in. Code cannot enforce agent use in each session.

alternatives.option: Show agent use with a marker that the coach hook writes
alternatives.rejected_because: The coach ignores each caller except GREEN. A missing marker then means a main-agent slice or a silent coach, and the check cannot tell them apart.

alternatives.option: Silence the coach on the habit-hooks markers for an unscanned file
alternatives.rejected_because: For a scanned extension, those markers show a misconfiguration that GREEN must report. The guard keys on the file extension instead.

alternatives.option: Run the script from the coach with uv run, and read a YAML config
alternatives.rejected_because: The coach is stdlib only, and two coach tests fail when it runs uv. A uv start on each write also adds delay.

alternatives.option: Deliver the signals as a sensor in a project-local habit-hooks plugin
alternatives.rejected_because: habit-hooks finds smells inside one file, and the signals judge folders and names. The engineer keeps the two jobs apart. A sensor also runs for six extensions only.

architecture.narration: The script sits in shared. The coach and VALIDATE in implement call it, and review mode and maintenance mode in architect read its output later. No plugin names a path in another plugin.

beats.text: shared/structure_signals.py reads the folder tree and the git comparison with the merge-base. It reports three signals, and it names each path that it did not analyse.
The findings JSON of habit-hooks is the seam. The script prints it, and each reader takes it: the coach, VALIDATE, and shared/habit_smells.py for the architect modes.

habit_coach.py keeps its GREEN filter and stays stdlib only. It gives structure signals for each extension, no smell output for an unscanned extension, and no repeat in a session. It has no cap at first.
VALIDATE runs the script on the slice, judges contract drift on the diff, and adds a Structure block to the attempt file, as the vocabulary agent adds its block.
verify_gate.py checks one effect that shows the agents ran each slice. The spike picks the effect, because the hook must not call the tracker.
